title: DIVERGING PREFERENCES: WHEN DO ANNOTATORS DISAGREE AND DO MODELS KNOW?

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the rate at which reward models and LLM-as-Judge methods predict decisive 'wins' rather than ties on dataset examples with high human annotator disagreement (diverging preferences) versus high-agreement examples.

Using prompt-based classification to identify 'Comply vs. Refuse' and 'Refusal vs. Refuse' response pairs, and measuring LLM-as-Judge win/loss rates to detect unfair preferences for compliance or specific refusal attributes (e.g., favoring refusals that prescribe solutions over those stating an inability to comply).

Classifying responses to underspecified prompts into 'overton' responses (providing multiple interpretations) or clarifying questions using GPT-4o, and comparing their average LLM-as-Judge scores to identify bias toward a single task-resolution strategy.
